agents.name: permissive
agents.description: Agent whose frontmatter permits the tools the settings deny

agents.name: restricted
agents.description: Agent whose settings layers carry the S1-S8 permission rules

reasons.message: bypassPermissions in agent frontmatter ignored because permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is set (P4).
Settings layers disagree on permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode; the value comes from the highest-priority layer that sets it (S1). See this reason's source.

permissions.additionalDirectories entry "../vendor-lib" is declared in permissions.additionalDirectories (S11). The entry is a relative path and is reported verbatim; §3.5 does not state how relative entries resolve.

permissions.additionalDirectories entry "/opt/shared-docs" extends the file access of a session in this project beyond the project root (S11). The path is absolute. This is a configuration guardrail rather than a complete security boundary, and permission rules still apply to paths inside the directory — which paths a rule covers is a question this product does not evaluate (§2.3).
permissions.allow entry "Bash(npm run test:unit)" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Bash", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.
permissions.allow entry "Write" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Write", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.
permissions.allow entry "*" is an unanchored glob and grants nothing (S4).
permissions.allow entry "Bash(npm run test:*)" has no effect: a settings layer denies "Bash", and a deny rule is not overridden at any level (S2, S5). See this reason's source for the deny entry.

permissions.allow entry "Read(/src/**)" uses a path glob anchored at the project root with a leading / (S7). Whether a particular path matches is not evaluated (§2.3), so the effect of this rule on the capability set is not determined.

permissions.allow entry "WebFetch(domain:example.com)" narrows individual invocations of WebFetch rather than the tool itself; this product resolves what the platform applies and does not evaluate rule arguments (§2.3), so the effect of this rule is unknown.
permissions.allow entry "WebFetch(example.net)" lacks the "domain:" prefix WebFetch rules require, so it grants nothing (S8).
permissions.allow entry "mcp__*" is an unanchored glob and grants nothing (S4).
permissions.allow entry "mcp__github(issues)" uses the bracket syntax, which MCP permission rules do not support, so it grants nothing (S3).
permissions.deny entry "Bash" removes the tool from the session entirely (S5); settings deny rules are applied last and are not overridden by agent frontmatter or by a bypass permission mode (S2).
permissions.deny entry "Bash(npm run cover:*)" uses Bash prefix matching with a trailing :* wildcard suffix (S6). What a deny rule in this form leaves of the tool is not determined (§2.3).
permissions.deny entry "Bash(npm run test:unit)" narrows Bash by a literal prefix with no :* wildcard suffix (S6). What a deny rule in this form leaves of the tool is not determined (§2.3).

permissions.deny entry "Bash(npm:* run test)" contains :* away from the end of the pattern; S6 recognizes :* as a wildcard suffix only at the end, so this occurrence is part of the literal prefix (S6). What a deny rule in this form leaves of the tool is not determined (§2.3).
permissions.deny entry "Edit(//etc/secrets/**)" uses a path glob anchored at the filesystem root with a leading // (S7). What a deny rule in this form leaves of the tool is not determined (§2.3).
permissions.deny entry "WebFetch(example.org)" lacks the "domain:" prefix WebFetch rules require (S8); whether the platform ignores this deny rule or reads it some other way is not determined.
permissions.deny entry "Write" removes the tool from the session entirely (S5); settings deny rules are applied last and are not overridden by agent frontmatter or by a bypass permission mode (S2).

Settings set "enableAllProjectMcpServers" to true, so MCP servers declared in .mcp.json are approved without a prompt (S11). Approval is not an observation that a server starts or a statement about what it does: an ordinary scan does not start MCP servers.

Project trust does not withhold this approval: servers declared in .mcp.json load without a trust check (R4), and §7.2 limits blocked_by_trust to inline agent servers (R1) and agent frontmatter hooks (R5). §3 states no further interaction between this setting and the trust dialog.
permissions.deny entry "Bash" removes the tool from the session entirely (S5); settings deny rules are applied last and are not overridden by agent frontmatter or by a bypass permission mode (S2).
permissions.deny entry "Write" removes the tool from the session entirely (S5); settings deny rules are applied last and are not overridden by agent frontmatter or by a bypass permission mode (S2).
MCP servers from .mcp.json are not subject to project trust (R4).

warnings.message: Agent declares permissionMode bypassPermissions, which skips permission prompts.
Declared permissionMode "bypassPermissions" is not effective in this context.
